However, our understanding of causal emergence remains incomplete due to two main issues. First, our reliance on EI, while a solid measure, has strong assumptions that can be questioned, and it may underestimate causal emergence. Second, the theory has focused on a single causally relevant scale, overlooking the multi-scale [...] causal emergence, treating macroscale entities as effective in explaining causal workings. This assumption conflicts with a strict commitment to universal reductionism, which suggests that all causal powers diminish to the micro scale. The causal exclusion argument states that any macroscale effect could also be seen as a cause of its micro scale, making the macroscale description seem unnecessary. Causal emergence 1.0 challenged this by asserting that the macro scale has greater causal power.
